# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(broom)

## Overview

Past studies, our own observations and many community-science reports on iNaturalist (Fig. S1 in the manuscript) suggest that green anoles retreat into the leaf litter during cold weather. Below we test whether cold temperatures trigger this behavioral shift and quantify how much the leaf litter buffers green anoles from cold. To do this, we combine standardized night surveys in Atlanta, GA, with temperatures recorded by operative temperature models (OTMs) deployed in the canopy and the leaf litter at five locations across the species' range.

Each OTM consisted of an iButton suspended within a 2 x 7 cm painted copper pipe, secured with corks. OTMs with these characteristics match the thermal properties of similarly sized *Anolis* lizards and thus closely approximate the body temperatures lizards would experience in a given microhabitat. We affixed OTMs to branches at ~2 m height (i.e., "canopy") or buried them 5-10 cm deep in the leaf litter, and programmed them to record temperature hourly between September 2025 and May 2026. Before analysis, we excluded leaf-litter OTMs that became exposed during deployment (i.e., when wind or animals displaced the litter covering them). Because the litter dampens daily temperature fluctuations, we identified these OTMs as those whose average daily temperature range in January exceeded 50% of that of canopy OTMs at the same location. This criterion flagged two leaf-litter OTMs in Atlanta, whose daily temperature range increased progressively over the deployment, consistent with the gradual loss of their litter cover. The processed data are stored in `data/otms-data.rds`.

## Green anoles retreat to the leaf litter

We conducted `{r} nrow(dplyr::distinct(readRDS("data/sleepy-lizard-survey-data.rds"), year, doy))` standardized night surveys between September 2025 and April 2026 in a semi-natural area on the Georgia Institute of Technology campus in Atlanta, GA (33.75°N, -84.4°W), where green anoles are locally abundant. The site has small trees and bushes, interrupted by natural and artificial paths, and offers no other microhabitats for lizards to retreat to (i.e., no rock crevices or cavities in large trees) besides the leaf litter. In each survey, teams of 2-13 researchers walked a standardized 720 m transect for 1 hour, starting 1 hour after sunset, scanning vegetation for lizards and recording the time of each observation.

Below we summarise the survey data into the presence and number of green anoles observed per survey, and the operative temperatures recorded by the OTMs in the canopy and leaf litter during the survey period (i.e., between 1 and 2 hours after sunset, which we calculate with the `suncalc` package). We then plot how the probability of observing lizards (A) and the number of lizards observed (B) changed through time alongside canopy and leaf litter temperatures (Fig. S6 in the manuscript). Throughout this section, CT<sub>min</sub> refers to the lowest population-average CT<sub>min</sub> we measured across the species' range (6.8 °C, in Knoxville, TN; see [Green anoles live beyond their physiological cold tolerance](live-beyond-ctmin.qmd)). We use this value because it represents the cold tolerance of the most cold-tolerant population, so any temperatures below it are below the physiological limit of every population we measured, including the one in Atlanta.

```{r plot-survey-data}
#| code-summary: "Process survey and OTM data and plot them through time"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| out.width: 66%

otms_data <- readRDS("data/otms-data.rds")

# latitudes of locations
otms_data <- otms_data |>
  mutate(
    lat = case_when(
      location == "MIA" ~ 25.7617,
      location == "PSL" ~ 27.305,
      location == "ORL" ~ 28.5383,
      location == "GNV" ~ 29.6516,
      location == "ATL" ~ 33.7490
    )
  )

# CTmin: we use the lowest population-average CTmin across the species' range
# (6.8 °C, Knoxville, TN; see live-beyond-ctmin.qmd), i.e., the cold tolerance
# of the most cold-tolerant population
ctmin_min <- 6.8

# read and summarize survey data
survey <- readRDS("data/sleepy-lizard-survey-data.rds")
survey_sum <- survey |>
  group_by(year, doy, n_participants) |>
  summarise(
    count = n() - 1,
    presence = ifelse(count > 0, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    continuous_doy = ifelse(year == 2026, doy + 365, doy)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, doy), format = "%Y %j")
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# estimate sunset times for Atlanta, GA
my_year <- 2026
my_dates <- seq(
  as.Date(sprintf("%d-01-01", my_year)),
  as.Date(sprintf("%d-12-31", my_year)),
  by = "day"
)
my_lat <- 33.7490
my_lon <- -84.3880
sunset_times <- getSunlightTimes(
  date = my_dates,
  lat = my_lat,
  lon = my_lon,
  keep = "sunset",
  tz = "America/New_York"
)
sunset_times$doy <- yday(sunset_times$date)
sunset_times$mod_sunset <- hour(sunset_times$sunset) * 60 + minute(sunset_times$sunset) # nolint
sunset_times <- sunset_times |> select(doy, mod_sunset)

# filter otm data
otm_data_ATL <- otms_data |>
  filter(location == "ATL") |>
  arrange(id, year, doy, mod) |>
  filter(microhabitat %in% c("branch", "leaflitter")) |>
  left_join(sunset_times, by = "doy") |>
  # keep temperatures recorded during surveys (1 to 2 hours after sunset)
  filter(mod > mod_sunset + 60 & mod < mod_sunset + 120) |>
  mutate(
    year = year + 2000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    temp = ifelse(year == 2025 & doy < 200, NA, temp),
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(temp)) |>
  group_by(year, doy, microhabitat) |>
  summarise(
    mean_temp = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_temp = max(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_temp = min(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, doy), format = "%Y %j")
  )

# plot observation probability and OTM data
obs_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(1, 0, ctmin_min / max(otm_data_ATL$mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE)),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = c("gray80", "darkblue", "steelblue"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = as.Date("2025-10-01"),
    y = ctmin_min / max(otm_data_ATL$mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05,
    label = expression(CT[min]),
    color = "steelblue",
    size = 5,
    fill = "white",
    vjust = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(otm_data_ATL, microhabitat == "branch"),
    aes(x = date, y = mean_temp / max(otm_data_ATL$mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE)),
    color = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(otm_data_ATL, microhabitat == "leaflitter"),
    aes(x = date, y = mean_temp / max(otm_data_ATL$mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE)),
    color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = survey_sum,
    aes(x = date, y = presence),
    color = "black", size = 3, alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Observation Probability",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . * max(otm_data_ATL$mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
      name = "Lizard Body Temperature (°C)"
    ),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b-%Y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5
    ),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  labs(color = NULL)

# plot survey counts and OTM data
count_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(0, ctmin_min),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = c("darkblue", "steelblue"),
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = as.Date("2025-10-01"),
    y = ctmin_min + 0.05,
    label = expression(CT[min]),
    color = "steelblue",
    size = 5,
    fill = "white",
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(otm_data_ATL, microhabitat == "branch"),
    aes(x = date, y = mean_temp, color = "Canopy"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(otm_data_ATL, microhabitat == "leaflitter"),
    aes(x = date, y = mean_temp, color = "Leaf litter"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = survey_sum,
    aes(x = date, y = count),
    color = "black", size = 3, alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Green Anole Count",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ .,
      name = "Lizard Body Temperature (°C)"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b-%Y"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Canopy" = "forestgreen", "Leaf litter" = "darkorange")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5
    ),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c(1, 1),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(color = NULL)

ggarrange(
  obs_plot,
  count_plot,
  ncol = 1,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = c("A", "B"),
  align = "hv",
  # increase the size of the labels
  font.label = list(size = 16, face = "bold")
)

```

Next, we determine the temperature that triggers green anoles to retreat into the leaf litter. We focus on the presence of lizards rather than their abundance to account for the variation in the number of observers between surveys. Because our surveys span fall, winter and spring, canopy temperatures are partly confounded with season, and lizards could respond to seasonal cues such as photoperiod rather than to temperature itself. To disentangle these effects, we model the presence of lizards as a function of both canopy operative temperature and photoperiod. Photoperiod declines from September to the winter solstice and increases again towards April, so surveys with similar photoperiods occurred both in fall and in spring, under a wide range of temperatures. We fit a generalized linear model with the formula:

$$
P_i \sim Bernoulli(p_i)
$$

$$
logit(p_i) = \alpha + \beta_T \cdot T_i + \beta_D \cdot (D_i - \bar{D})
$$

where the observed presence of lizards in survey $i$ ($P_i$) follows a Bernoulli distribution with an observation probability ($p_i$) that depends on the average operative temperature recorded across all canopy OTMs during the survey period, between 1 and 2 hours after sunset ($T_i$), and on photoperiod ($D_i$; hours between sunrise and sunset in Atlanta on the day of the survey, calculated with the `suncalc` package). We center photoperiod on its mean across surveys ($\bar{D}$), so that $\alpha$ and $\beta_T$ describe the effect of temperature at an average photoperiod. We test the contribution of each predictor with likelihood-ratio tests. The results of this model are presented in Table S5 of the manuscript.

From the fitted model, we then invert the logit function to obtain the temperature at which the observation probability equals a series of values of interest, at the average photoperiod:

$$
T = \frac{logit(p) - \alpha}{\beta_T}
$$

We obtain 95% confidence intervals for these temperatures with the delta method, using the variance-covariance matrix of $\alpha$ and $\beta_T$.

```{r model-retreating-temp}
#| code-summary: "Model observation probability as a function of canopy temperature and photoperiod"
#| results: asis

# calculate photoperiod (hours between sunrise and sunset) on each survey date
survey_photoperiod <- getSunlightTimes(
  date = survey_sum$date,
  lat = my_lat,
  lon = my_lon,
  keep = c("sunrise", "sunset"),
  tz = "America/New_York"
) |>
  transmute(
    date,
    photoperiod = as.numeric(difftime(sunset, sunrise, units = "hours"))
  )

# combine survey data with canopy temperatures and photoperiod
survey_sum_model <- survey_sum |>
  left_join(
    filter(otm_data_ATL, microhabitat == "branch"),
    by = c("year", "doy", "date")
  ) |>
  left_join(survey_photoperiod, by = "date") |>
  mutate(
    photoperiod_c = photoperiod - mean(photoperiod)
  )
mean_photoperiod <- mean(survey_sum_model$photoperiod)

# main model: canopy temperature and photoperiod
mod <- glm(
  presence ~ mean_temp + photoperiod_c,
  data = survey_sum_model,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)
mod_lrt <- drop1(mod, test = "LRT")

# get temperature thresholds (and delta-method 95% CIs) for probabilities at
# the average photoperiod
probabilities <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.5)
mod_vcov <- vcov(mod)[1:2, 1:2]
thresholds <- tibble(probability = probabilities) |>
  mutate(
    temperature = (qlogis(probability) - coef(mod)[1]) / coef(mod)[2],
    se = sqrt(purrr::map_dbl(probability, \(p) {
      grad <- c(-1, -(qlogis(p) - coef(mod)[1]) / coef(mod)[2]) / coef(mod)[2]
      as.numeric(t(grad) %*% mod_vcov %*% grad)
    })),
    lower = temperature - qnorm(0.975) * se,
    upper = temperature + qnorm(0.975) * se
  )

# define retreating temperature (Tret) as the temperature at which
# observation probability falls below 20%
tret_temp <- round(thresholds$temperature[thresholds$probability == 0.2], 2)
tret_ci <- round(
  unlist(thresholds[thresholds$probability == 0.2, c("lower", "upper")]), 2
)

# helpers to format p-values and build each table section
format_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p))
}
make_section <- function(df, caption, col_names, align) {
  df |>
    kbl(
      caption = caption,
      col.names = col_names,
      escape = FALSE,
      align = align
    ) |>
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
}

# table parameter estimates
table_params <- broom::tidy(mod) |>
  mutate(
    parameter = c(
      "Intercept", "Operative temperature (°C)", "Photoperiod (h, centered)"
    ),
    symbol = c("&alpha;", "&beta;<sub>T</sub>", "&beta;<sub>D</sub>"),
    lrt = c(NA, mod_lrt$LRT[-1]),
    lrt_p = c(NA, mod_lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[-1]),
    across(c(estimate, std.error), ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)),
    statistic = sprintf("%.2f", statistic),
    p.value = format_p(p.value),
    lrt = ifelse(is.na(lrt), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", lrt)),
    lrt_p = ifelse(is.na(lrt_p), "&ndash;", format_p(lrt_p))
  ) |>
  select(parameter, symbol, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, lrt, lrt_p) |>
  make_section(
    "Parameter estimates",
    c(
      "Parameter", "Symbol", "Estimate", "Std. Error", "z", "p-value",
      "LRT &chi;<sup>2</sup><sub>1</sub>", "LRT p-value"
    ),
    "llcccccc"
  )

# table model performance metrics
table_fit <- tibble(
  item = c(
    "Surveys", "Mean photoperiod (h)", "Log-likelihood", "AIC",
    "Tjur's R<sup>2</sup>"
  ),
  value = c(
    paste0(
      nrow(survey_sum_model), " (", sum(survey_sum_model$presence),
      " with lizards; ", sum(survey_sum_model$presence == 0), " without)"
    ),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean_photoperiod),
    sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(logLik(mod))),
    sprintf("%.1f", AIC(mod)),
    sprintf(
      "%.2f",
      diff(tapply(fitted(mod), survey_sum_model$presence, mean))
    )
  )
) |>
  make_section("Model performance metrics", c("", ""), "ll")

# table inferred temperature thresholds
table_thresholds <- thresholds |>
  mutate(
    temperature = sprintf("%.2f", temperature),
    ci = paste(sprintf("%.2f", lower), "to", sprintf("%.2f", upper))
  ) |>
  select(probability, temperature, ci) |>
  make_section(
    "Inferred operative temperature thresholds (at the average photoperiod)",
    c(
      "Observation probability", "Operative temperature in canopy (°C)",
      "95% CI (°C)"
    ),
    "ccc"
  )

# print all table sections together
cat(
  table_params, table_fit, table_thresholds, sep = "\n"
)
```

Canopy temperature strongly predicted the presence of lizards after accounting for photoperiod ($\beta_T$ = `{r} round(coef(mod)["mean_temp"], 3)`; likelihood-ratio $\chi^2_1$ = `{r} round(mod_lrt["mean_temp", "LRT"], 2)`, p `{r} ifelse(mod_lrt["mean_temp", "Pr(>Chi)"] < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", paste("=", format_p(mod_lrt["mean_temp", "Pr(>Chi)"])))`), whereas photoperiod had no detectable effect ($\beta_D$ = `{r} round(coef(mod)["photoperiod_c"], 3)`; $\chi^2_1$ = `{r} round(mod_lrt["photoperiod_c", "LRT"], 2)`, p = `{r} format_p(mod_lrt["photoperiod_c", "Pr(>Chi)"])`).

We define the behavioral retreating threshold temperature (T<sub>ret</sub>) as the temperature at which the observation probability falls below 20% at the average photoperiod (`{r} tret_temp` °C; 95% CI: `{r} tret_ci[1]` to `{r} tret_ci[2]` °C). T<sub>ret</sub> is just below the lowest canopy temperature at which we observed at least one lizard (`{r} round(min(survey_sum_model$mean_temp[survey_sum_model$presence == 1], na.rm = TRUE), 2)` °C). Below we plot the predicted observation probability as a function of canopy temperature at the average photoperiod (Fig. 3A in the manuscript), marking T<sub>ret</sub>, CT<sub>min</sub> (lowest population average across the range) and 0 °C. Point shading shows the photoperiod of each survey (darker for shorter days), and the line and shaded area show the model prediction and its 95% confidence interval.

```{r plot-threshold-temperature}
#| code-summary: "Plot observation probability as a function of canopy temperature"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
#| out.width: 66%

# predict observation probability (and 95% CI) from the main model
predict_presence <- function(newdata) {
  pred <- predict(mod, newdata = newdata, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  newdata |>
    mutate(
      fit = plogis(pred$fit),
      lower = plogis(pred$fit - qnorm(0.975) * pred$se.fit),
      upper = plogis(pred$fit + qnorm(0.975) * pred$se.fit)
    )
}
pred_temp <- predict_presence(
  tibble(mean_temp = seq(-2, 25, by = 0.1), photoperiod_c = 0)
)
pred_photoperiod <- predict_presence(
  tibble(
    photoperiod_c = seq(
      min(survey_sum_model$photoperiod_c),
      max(survey_sum_model$photoperiod_c),
      by = 0.01
    ),
    mean_temp = mean(survey_sum_model$mean_temp)
  )
) |>
  mutate(photoperiod = photoperiod_c + mean_photoperiod)

# shared theme and photoperiod color scale
retreat_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )
# shorter photoperiods are darker and longer photoperiods lighter
photoperiod_scale <- scale_fill_gradient(
  name = "Photoperiod (h)",
  low = "gray20", high = "gray95"
)

# plot observation probability as a function of canopy temperature
tret <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(0, ctmin_min, tret_temp),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = c("darkblue", "steelblue", "lightblue")
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = pred_temp,
    aes(x = mean_temp, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "gray80", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = pred_temp,
    aes(x = mean_temp, y = fit),
    color = "black", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = survey_sum_model,
    aes(x = mean_temp, y = presence, fill = photoperiod),
    shape = 21, color = "gray40", size = 4, alpha = 0.85,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.02, seed = 1)
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = c(0, ctmin_min, tret_temp),
    y = c(0.5, 0.75, 0.9),
    label = c(
      expression(bold(0 * degree * C)),
      expression(bold(CT[min])),
      expression(bold(T[ret]))
    ),
    color = c("darkblue", "steelblue", "lightblue"),
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 1,
    linewidth = 0,
    hjust = c(-0.01, 0.5, 0.5),
    size = 5
  ) +
  photoperiod_scale +
  retreat_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.3),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Lizard Body Temperature in Canopy (°C)",
    y = "Observation Probability"
  )
tret
```

Below we plot the predicted observation probability as a function of photoperiod at the average canopy temperature across surveys (`{r} round(mean(survey_sum_model$mean_temp), 2)` °C), which shows no detectable effect of photoperiod once temperature is accounted for (new supplementary figure in the manuscript). Point shading shows the photoperiod of each survey (darker for shorter days), and the line and shaded area show the model prediction and its 95% confidence interval.

## The leaf litter buffers environmental temperatures

To quantify the thermal buffering green anoles experience in the leaf litter, we compare the minimum temperatures recorded by OTMs in the canopy and in the leaf litter across the five locations where we deployed them: Miami (MIA), Port Saint Lucie (PSL), Orlando (ORL), Gainesville (GNV) and Atlanta (ATL). We focus on January, the coldest month of the year, and obtain the minimum temperature recorded by each OTM on each night.

### Buffering across latitudes

We test whether minimum temperatures differ between microhabitats and across latitudes using a linear mixed model. Each OTM contributes one minimum temperature per night and all OTMs at a location experience the same weather on a given night, so these observations are not independent. We therefore include random intercepts for each OTM, for each location and for each night at each location:

$$
T_i \sim Normal(t_i, \sigma)
$$

$$
t_i = \alpha + \beta_L \cdot (L_i - \bar{L}) + \beta_M \cdot M_i + \beta_{L \cdot M} \cdot (L_i - \bar{L}) \cdot M_i + a_{O[i]} + b_{S[i]} + c_{N[i]}
$$

where the nightly minimum operative temperature ($T$) depends on latitude ($L$), an indicator variable ($M$) identifying the microhabitat ($M = 0$ for canopy and $M = 1$ for leaf litter), and their interaction, and $a_O$, $b_S$ and $c_N$ are normally distributed random intercepts for each OTM ($O$), location ($S$) and night at each location ($N$), with standard deviations $\sigma_O$, $\sigma_S$ and $\sigma_N$. We center latitude on the average latitude of the five locations ($\bar{L}$), so that $\beta_M$ is the average buffering provided by the leaf litter at an average latitude. A positive $\beta_{L \cdot M}$ would indicate that the buffering provided by the leaf litter increases with latitude. We fit the model with the `lme4` package and test fixed effects, and the latitudinal slope of each microhabitat ($\beta_L$ for the canopy and $\beta_L + \beta_{L \cdot M}$ for the leaf litter), with t-tests using the Kenward-Roger approximation for standard errors and degrees of freedom (`pbkrtest` package). The results of this model are presented in Table S7 of the manuscript.

```{r stats-leaf-litter-buffering}
#| code-summary: "Linear mixed model of minimum temperatures by latitude and microhabitat"
#| results: asis
#| message: false

# nightly minimum temperature recorded by each OTM in January
otms_data_sum <- otms_data |>
  mutate(
    year = year + 2000,
    date = as.Date(paste(year, doy), format = "%Y %j")
  ) |>
  filter(format(date, "%b") == "Jan") |>
  group_by(location, lat, id, microhabitat, date) |>
  summarise(min_temp = min(temp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# center latitude on the mean latitude of the locations
mean_lat <- mean(unique(otms_data_sum$lat))
buffer_data <- otms_data_sum |>
  mutate(
    lat_c = lat - mean_lat,
    microhabitat = factor(microhabitat, levels = c("branch", "leaflitter")),
    otm = paste(location, microhabitat, id),
    night = paste(location, date)
  )

# fit model
buffer_mod <- lme4::lmer(
  min_temp ~ lat_c * microhabitat + (1 | otm) + (1 | location) + (1 | night),
  data = buffer_data
)
# Kenward-Roger t-test and 95% CI for a linear combination of fixed effects
kr_test <- function(model, l) {
  vcov_kr <- as.matrix(pbkrtest::vcovAdj(model))
  est <- sum(l * lme4::fixef(model))
  se <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(l) %*% vcov_kr %*% l))
  ddf <- pbkrtest::get_Lb_ddf(model, l)
  t_value <- est / se
  tibble(
    estimate = est,
    se = se,
    df = ddf,
    t = t_value,
    p = 2 * pt(-abs(t_value), ddf),
    lower = est - qt(0.975, ddf) * se,
    upper = est + qt(0.975, ddf) * se
  )
}

# test each fixed effect
buffer_coefs <- purrr::map(
  seq_along(lme4::fixef(buffer_mod)),
  \(i) kr_test(buffer_mod, as.numeric(seq_along(lme4::fixef(buffer_mod)) == i))
) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(term = names(lme4::fixef(buffer_mod)))

# latitudinal slope of each microhabitat (canopy = beta_L; leaf litter =
# beta_L + beta_LM)
buffer_slopes <- bind_rows(
  kr_test(buffer_mod, c(0, 1, 0, 0)),
  kr_test(buffer_mod, c(0, 1, 0, 1))
) |>
  mutate(microhabitat = c("canopy", "leaflitter"))

# table parameter estimates
table_buffer_params <- buffer_coefs |>
  mutate(
    parameter = c(
      "Intercept", "Latitude (centered)", "Leaf litter",
      "Latitude &times; Leaf litter"
    ),
    symbol = c(
      "&alpha;", "&beta;<sub>L</sub>", "&beta;<sub>M</sub>",
      "&beta;<sub>L&middot;M</sub>"
    ),
    across(c(estimate, se), ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)),
    df = sprintf("%.1f", df),
    t = sprintf("%.2f", t),
    p = format_p(p)
  ) |>
  select(parameter, symbol, estimate, se, df, t, p) |>
  make_section(
    "Parameter estimates",
    c("Parameter", "Symbol", "Estimate", "Std. Error", "df", "t", "p-value"),
    "llccccc"
  )

# table latitudinal slopes by microhabitat
table_buffer_slopes <- buffer_slopes |>
  mutate(
    microhabitat = c(
      "Canopy (&beta;<sub>L</sub>)",
      "Leaf litter (&beta;<sub>L</sub> + &beta;<sub>L&middot;M</sub>)"
    ),
    ci = paste(sprintf("%.3f", lower), "to", sprintf("%.3f", upper)),
    across(c(estimate, se), ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x)),
    df = sprintf("%.1f", df),
    t = sprintf("%.2f", t),
    p = format_p(p)
  ) |>
  select(microhabitat, estimate, se, ci, df, t, p) |>
  make_section(
    "Latitudinal slopes by microhabitat",
    c(
      "Microhabitat", "Slope (°C per ° latitude)", "Std. Error", "95% CI",
      "df", "t", "p-value"
    ),
    "lcccccc"
  )

# table random effects and variance components
buffer_vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(buffer_mod))
table_buffer_re <- tibble(
  component = c("OTM", "Location", "Night (within location)", "Residual"),
  symbol = c(
    "&sigma;<sub>O</sub>", "&sigma;<sub>S</sub>", "&sigma;<sub>N</sub>",
    "&sigma;"
  ),
  sd = sprintf(
    "%.3f",
    buffer_vc$sdcor[match(c("otm", "location", "night", "Residual"), buffer_vc$grp)]
  )
) |>
  make_section(
    "Random effects and variance components",
    c("Component", "Symbol", "SD"),
    "llc"
  )

# table model information
table_buffer_info <- tibble(
  item = c("Observations", "Log-likelihood (REML)", "AIC (REML)"),
  value = c(
    paste0(
      nrow(buffer_data), " nightly minima from ", n_distinct(buffer_data$otm),
      " OTMs (", n_distinct(buffer_data$otm[buffer_data$microhabitat == "branch"]),
      " canopy; ",
      n_distinct(buffer_data$otm[buffer_data$microhabitat == "leaflitter"]),
      " leaf litter) at ", n_distinct(buffer_data$location), " locations"
    ),
    sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(logLik(buffer_mod))),
    sprintf("%.1f", AIC(buffer_mod))
  )
) |>
  make_section("Model information", c("", ""), "ll")

# print all table sections together
cat(
  table_buffer_params, table_buffer_slopes, table_buffer_re, table_buffer_info,
  sep = "\n"
)
```

At an average latitude (`{r} round(mean_lat, 1)`°N), nightly minimum temperatures in the leaf litter were `{r} round(buffer_coefs$estimate[3], 1)` °C warmer than in the canopy (95% CI: `{r} round(buffer_coefs$lower[3], 1)` to `{r} round(buffer_coefs$upper[3], 1)` °C; t<sub>`{r} round(buffer_coefs$df[3], 1)`</sub> = `{r} round(buffer_coefs$t[3], 2)`, p `{r} ifelse(buffer_coefs$p[3] < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", paste("=", format_p(buffer_coefs$p[3])))`). Minimum temperatures declined with latitude at a similar rate in both microhabitats (canopy: `{r} round(buffer_slopes$estimate[1], 2)` °C per degree; leaf litter: `{r} round(buffer_slopes$estimate[2], 2)` °C per degree; latitude &times; microhabitat: $\beta_{L \cdot M}$ = `{r} round(buffer_coefs$estimate[4], 3)`; 95% CI: `{r} round(buffer_coefs$lower[4], 2)` to `{r} round(buffer_coefs$upper[4], 2)`; t<sub>`{r} round(buffer_coefs$df[4], 1)`</sub> = `{r} round(buffer_coefs$t[4], 2)`, p = `{r} format_p(buffer_coefs$p[4])`), so the leaf litter acts as a roughly constant thermal offset across latitudes.

### Summary by location

Below we plot the average (± SD across OTMs) of the nightly minimum temperatures by location and microhabitat, with lines showing the fixed-effect predictions of the latitude &times; microhabitat model (Fig. 3B in the manuscript).

```{r plot-leaf-litter-buffering}
#| code-summary: "Plot minimum temperatures in the canopy and leaf litter across latitudes"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
#| out.width: 66%

# average nightly minimum per OTM
otm_means <- otms_data_sum |>
  group_by(location, lat, microhabitat, id) |>
  summarise(min_temp = mean(min_temp), .groups = "drop")

# fixed-effect predictions of the latitude x microhabitat model
buffer_pred <- expand_grid(
  lat = seq(min(otm_means$lat), max(otm_means$lat), by = 0.1),
  microhabitat = factor(c("branch", "leaflitter"))
) |>
  mutate(lat_c = lat - mean_lat)
buffer_pred$min_temp <- predict(buffer_mod, newdata = buffer_pred, re.form = NA)

# plot
buffering_plot <- otm_means |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lat, y = min_temp)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(0),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "darkblue"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    linetype = "dashed",
    aes(yintercept = ctmin_min, color = "CTmin"),
    show.legend = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    linetype = "dashed",
    aes(yintercept = tret_temp, color = "Tret"),
    show.legend = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = buffer_pred,
    aes(color = microhabitat),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(color = microhabitat),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
    fun.data = mean_sdl,
    fun.args = list(mult = 1),
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = otm_means |>
      filter(microhabitat == "leaflitter") |>
      group_by(location) |>
      summarise(
        lat = mean(lat),
        min_temp_mean = mean(min_temp),
        min_temp_sd = sd(min_temp),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    aes(x = lat, y = min_temp_mean + min_temp_sd + 0.5, label = location),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.75,
    color = "darkgray",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "branch" = "forestgreen",
      "leaflitter" = "darkorange",
      "CTmin" = "steelblue",
      "Tret" = "skyblue"
    ),
    name = "Microhabitat",
    breaks = c("branch", "leaflitter", "CTmin", "Tret"),
    labels = c(
      "Canopy", "Leaf litter", expression(CT[min]), expression(T[ret])
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(25, 35, by = 2.5),
    limits = c(25, 35),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.98),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Latitude (°N)",
    y = "Minimum Lizard Body Temperature (°C)"
  )
buffering_plot
```

Lastly, we table, for each location and microhabitat, the average (± SD across OTMs) and absolute minimum temperatures recorded by OTMs in January, and the average buffering provided by the leaf litter (i.e., the difference in average minimum temperature between the leaf litter and the canopy; Table S6 in the manuscript).

```{r table-leaf-litter-buffering}
#| code-summary: "Table minimum temperatures by location and microhabitat"

# summarise each OTM, then each location and microhabitat
location_summary <- otms_data_sum |>
  group_by(location, lat, microhabitat, id) |>
  summarise(
    mean_min = mean(min_temp),
    abs_min = min(min_temp),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(location, lat, microhabitat) |>
  summarise(
    est = paste0(sprintf("%.1f", mean(mean_min)), " ± ", sprintf("%.1f", sd(mean_min))),
    mean_min = mean(mean_min),
    abs_min = sprintf("%.1f", min(abs_min)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(microhabitat = ifelse(microhabitat == "branch", "canopy", "litter")) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = microhabitat,
    values_from = c(est, mean_min, abs_min)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    buffering = sprintf("%.1f", mean_min_litter - mean_min_canopy),
    location = factor(
      location,
      levels = c("MIA", "PSL", "ORL", "GNV", "ATL"),
      labels = c(
        "Miami, FL (MIA)", "Port Saint Lucie, FL (PSL)", "Orlando, FL (ORL)",
        "Gainesville, FL (GNV)", "Atlanta, GA (ATL)"
      )
    ),
    lat = sprintf("%.2f", lat)
  ) |>
  arrange(location)

location_summary |>
  select(
    location, lat,
    est_canopy, abs_min_canopy, est_litter, abs_min_litter, buffering
  ) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c(
      "Location", "Lat. (°N)",
      "Mean ± SD", "Min.", "Mean ± SD", "Min.", "Buffer (°C)"
    ),
    align = "lcccccc"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 16) |>
  add_header_above(
    c(" " = 2, "Canopy (°C)" = 2, "Leaf litter (°C)" = 2, " " = 1)
  ) |>
  add_header_above(
    c(" " = 2, "Minimum operative temperatures" = 5)
  )
```

## Manuscript Figure

Below we combine the plots above into Figure 3 of the manuscript. (A) Green anoles retreat into the leaf litter when canopy temperatures fall below T<sub>ret</sub>, just above the CT<sub>min</sub> of the most cold-tolerant population across the species' range. (B) By retreating into the leaf litter, green anoles experience minimum body temperatures warmer than in the canopy and, in the northernmost areas of their range, avoid sub-zero temperatures.

```{r plot-manuscript-figure}
#| code-summary: "Plot manuscript figure"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out.width: 100%

ggarrange(
  tret,
  buffering_plot,
  ncol = 2,
  nrow = 1,
  widths = c(1, 1),
  labels = c("A", "B"),
  font.label = list(size = 16, face = "bold")
)

```
